title: {coworker} sent your partner screenshots of you taking credit for their work. Your partner is typing…

outcomes.text: You explain everything. Your partner goes quiet, then: 'Thanks for not lying to me too.'
Your partner needs a few days. They come back, a little warier.
They believe you. For now.

later.text: Remember calling {coworker}'s screenshots fake? {coworker} sent the originals, with timestamps. Your partner replied with one word: 'wow.'

outcomes.text: {coworker} shrugs: 'Fair's fair.' Now you both have something on each other.

title: {employer}'s client list is still in your old work email. A rival firm offers C$2,500 for it.

outcomes.text: C$2,500 lands. The rival firm sends a fruit basket. It's a very big fruit basket.

later.text: Remember {employer}'s client list? Their lawyers traced the download to your login.
later.headline: BREAKING: {employer} goes after former employee {name} over a client list that 'walked out the door.' {name} declined to comment.

outcomes.text: Deleted. You feel ten pounds lighter and C$2,500 poorer.

later.text: Remember deleting {employer}'s client list? Their IT team noticed. They called with a consulting gig.

outcomes.text: {employer} says 'thanks, weirdly.' Your reference now says 'honest to a fault.'

title: Fresh off your promotion, {boss} asks you to sign off on some very optimistic numbers. 'Just this quarter.'

options.label: Sign it
options.cost: Your name on the creative math

outcomes.text: You sign. {boss} squeezes your shoulder. A C$2,000 'performance bonus' appears.

later.text: Remember the numbers you signed for {boss}? An auditor is in the lobby, asking for you.

outcomes.text: 'I'm not comfortable signing that.' {boss} says 'noted' in a way that echoes.

later.text: Remember refusing {boss}'s numbers? Someone else signed. The audit took them, not you. You got their desk.

outcomes.text: HR thanks you. {boss} is 'on leave.' The office is very quiet around you.
HR 'looks into it.' {boss} finds out who called. Your next review will be interesting.

title: An auditor wants to know who signed off on the quarter's numbers. Your signature is on page one.

outcomes.text: The auditor nods. Your boss is walked out. You're 'reassigned' to the supply closet desk.

options.label: Confess everything
options.cost: A fine and a few hours

outcomes.text: You talk for an hour. Two hours in holding at the 114½ and a fine. You sleep fine, for once.
Your lawyer says 'no comment' beautifully. The audit drags on and then drifts away.
It doesn't drift. Fined, headlined, and locked off the gig board for a while.

title: Your partner's birthday party is at {place}, the place you're banned from.

options.label: Sneak in the back
options.get: The toast, the cake, the night

outcomes.text: The kitchen door works. You make the toast. Nobody important saw.
Security remembers you. Your partner watches you get walked out, cake in hand.

options.label: Throw a second party
options.cost: C$600 and a lot of texting

outcomes.text: Half the guests come to yours after. Your partner calls it 'the better party.'

options.label: Tell them why you can't come

outcomes.text: 'You're banned? From there?' They laugh for a full minute, then go without you.

later.text: Remember missing the party at {place}? Your partner's friends threw you a 'banned' party at your place. Iconic.

title: The opposition found your campus exam record, peeking and all. Your candidate wants a statement by noon.

outcomes.text: 'I cut corners in school. I don't now.' It plays better than anyone expected.
'I cut corners in school.' The clip is everywhere, minus the part where you apologize.

options.label: Call it a smear
options.get: A news cycle that moves on

outcomes.text: You call it a smear. It works, for now.

later.text: Remember calling your exam record a smear? Your old professor posted the timestamps.
later.headline: Developing: a professor posts exam logs contradicting {name}, who called them 'a smear' last week. The campaign says it's 'moving forward.'

outcomes.text: You step back for a week. The candidate sends a handwritten note. It's nicer than you expected.

title: Your crew heard about your scratch-card win. One of them needs C$1,000 'for rent, I swear.'

outcomes.text: You send it. They send twelve heart emojis.

later.text: Remember the C$1,000 you lent? Paid back with interest and a bagel.

outcomes.text: You send it. They go quiet.

later.text: Remember the loan? Your friend's new sneakers say it's not coming back.

outcomes.text: 'It's what I can do.' They take it, gratefully. Mostly.
'I can't right now, sorry.' The next hang is a little cold.

title: Vivian heard you collect gossip. 'Give me your best piece for the Big Screen and a promotion is yours.'

outcomes.text: It airs at 9. Vivian smiles for the first time since you met her.

later.text: Remember the gossip you gave Vivian? The person it was about found out it came from you.

outcomes.text: It airs. It's juicy. It's also fiction.

later.text: Remember the gossip you made up for Vivian? It was fact-checked. By the person it was about.
later.headline: BREAKING: Clout TV pulls a segment after its subject proves it was invented. Producers point at a junior staffer, {name}.

outcomes.text: Vivian says 'disappointing' and means it. Your sources send you better tea.

title: {boss} saw you on Lola's Blotter. 'So. The 114½ Precinct. Want to explain?'

outcomes.text: {boss} laughs. 'Honestly? I've done worse.' You're fine.
{boss} nods slowly and writes something down.
'A mix-up. Wrong person.' {boss} buys it.

later.text: Remember the 'mix-up'? Sgt. Bev came by the office to return your belt. In front of everyone.

outcomes.text: Your telling of the holding cell is a hit. The office calls you 'the convict' with love.

title: Your ex just walked into {employer} as a customer. They asked for you. Loudly.

outcomes.text: You take their order like a stranger. They tip 20%. Somehow that hurts more.
Your work friend handles it. Then tells everyone. Then buys you a coffee.
Everyone films it. You're a meme by lunch, a good one.

title: {boss} heard you aced an exam. Their nephew's exam is tomorrow: 'Just help him with the answers.'

outcomes.text: He gets an A. {boss} slips you C$600 'for your time.'

later.text: Remember helping {boss}'s nephew? He got caught. He said your name immediately.

outcomes.text: Three hours of flashcards. He gets it, sort of.

later.text: Remember tutoring {boss}'s nephew? He passed, honestly. {boss} hasn't stopped mentioning it.

outcomes.text: 'I'm swamped, sorry.' {boss} says 'of course' and does not mean it.

title: The wallet you kept? It belonged to your partner's cousin. They're telling the story at dinner tonight.

options.label: Confess at dinner
options.cost: C$600 and a very long silence

outcomes.text: You hand over C$600 and the truth. The cousin laughs. Your partner doesn't, yet.
You nod along to the story of the stolen wallet. You have seconds of everything.

later.text: Remember the cousin's wallet? They found you on the park camera footage. Dinner plans are cancelled indefinitely.

outcomes.text: You ask about everyone's fantasy football teams. It works. Barely.

title: Vivian found your old fake 'Dunk Daniels is coming' post. 'Is this who we hired for the newsroom?'

outcomes.text: 'I needed rent money.' Vivian: 'Relatable. Don't do it again.'
Vivian doesn't laugh. She does write something down.

options.label: Pitch 'I faked hype' as a story

outcomes.text: 'How I Lied To 400 People For C$900' does huge numbers. Vivian takes half the credit.

title: The rumor you started at work is now an opposition attack on your campaign: 'This is who they hire?'

outcomes.text: Your apology is short and real. The coworker accepts it on camera. The story dies.
You double down. Your supporters love it.

later.text: Remember doubling down on the office rumor? The coworker went on Real Clout FM. They were charming.
later.headline: Developing: the coworker at the center of {name}'s office rumor tells Real Clout FM it was 'made up over a vending machine.'

outcomes.text: You say nothing. The story fades in four days, slowly.

title: Your subtenant left a closet of 'designer' bags behind. A buyer offers C$1,500, no questions.

outcomes.text: C$1,500 and an empty closet.

later.text: Remember the bags? They were your subtenant's mom's. She has a lawyer and a very loud voice.

outcomes.text: You box them up and mail them back. It costs C$40 in postage. Worth it.

later.text: Remember returning the bags? Your ex-subtenant's mom sent a C$500 thank-you card.

outcomes.text: You keep the nicest one. It's fake. Obviously.

title: Lola noticed you always know things first. She wants you as an 'anonymous source.' Paid.

outcomes.text: Lola sends C$800 and a kiss emoji. You're on the inside now.

later.text: Remember becoming Lola's source? Your name leaked in her group chat. Your crew is not amused.

outcomes.text: 'Babe, your loss.' It isn't.

options.label: Ask for a favor instead
options.get: A Lola favor in the bank

outcomes.text: Lola runs a glowing item about you instead. 'We'll talk.' You will.

title: HR is checking résumés and exam records company-wide. Yours has two stories that don't match.

options.label: Come clean to HR
options.get: No more stories to keep up

outcomes.text: HR thanks you for 'getting ahead of it.' A note goes in your file. A small one.

options.label: 'Fix' the paperwork
options.cost: C$400 to a guy who knows a guy

outcomes.text: The guy fixes it. The paperwork matches now.

later.text: Remember fixing your paperwork? The registrar keeps copies. So does HR, now.

outcomes.text: Nobody checks yours. This time.
They check. 'Let's talk Monday.' Your weekend is ruined.

title: A new hire asks you, straight up: 'Are you the one who reports people?'

outcomes.text: They nod slowly. Maybe they get it. Maybe they'll tell everyone. Both, probably.

options.label: Deny it
options.cost: A lie with a short shelf life

outcomes.text: 'Me? Never.' They believe you until lunch.
'Only on Tuesdays.' They laugh. The question hangs there anyway.

title: {place} banned you. Now it wants to promote your business, after an apology video.

outcomes.text: Your apology does numbers. Business is up, and the owner sends a free drink voucher.
'No apologies.' You feel great about it for an hour.

options.label: Apologize now, trash them later
options.get: The money and the last word

outcomes.text: You film a lovely apology. C$800. You have plans for next week.

later.text: Remember your apology video for {place}? You trashed them a week later. The owner posted both side by side.

title: Since your candidate won, {employer} wants you to ask City Hall for a 'small zoning favor.'

outcomes.text: One call. The favor goes through. The bonus arrives in an envelope, which is never a good sign.

later.text: Remember the zoning favor for {employer}? Lola's Blotter connected the dots.
later.headline: BREAKING: a zoning change at City Hall traces back to a phone call from {name}, who works for the company it helped. Developing.

outcomes.text: 'I don't do favors.' Your boss is cold to you for exactly one week.

options.label: Point them to the public process

outcomes.text: You send them the zoning board's forms. It takes three months. It goes through, legitimately.

title: {coworker} is at the next table on your date night, and they're telling your date about you.

outcomes.text: You walk over and apologize, for real. {coworker} is stunned. Your date is impressed.
'Let's try the place down the street.' Your date clocks it. Says nothing. Yet.
You tell your side, louder. The waiter brings everyone free dessert to make it stop.

title: Working late. {coworker} brings your exact coffee order: 'Is it weird if this feels like a date?'

options.label: Say it's a date
options.get: Butterflies, a reason to come in

outcomes.text: 'Okay. It's a date.' {coworker} grins at the spreadsheet for the rest of the night.

later.text: Remember your late night with {coworker}? HR has booked 'a quick chat' with you both. Room 3B. Bring nothing.

options.label: Keep it friends
options.riskWhy: Friends for life is friends for life

outcomes.text: 'You're my favorite person here. Let's keep it that way.' {coworker} laughs, a little too fast. Still your person.
You let it hang there. {coworker} takes your Saturday shift without being asked.

later.text: Remember letting {coworker} think it was going somewhere? They worked it out. The whole break room knows.

title: HR's 'quick chat' about you and {coworker}. There's a form. It has a box for 'nature of relationship.'

options.label: Fill in the form, honestly
options.cost: Your love life in a filing cabinet

outcomes.text: You tick 'dating.' HR stamps it. {coworker} squeezes your hand under the table. Weirdly romantic.

options.label: Say you're just friends
options.cost: Lying to HR, with {coworker} next to you

outcomes.text: 'Just friends.' {coworker} goes very still. HR writes something down.

later.text: Remember telling HR you and {coworker} were 'just friends'? The lobby camera disagrees. So does Lola.
later.headline: Two coworkers at a certain Astoria employer are 'just friends,' per HR. Per the lobby camera, less so. One of them is {name}.

options.label: End it before it's a problem

outcomes.text: You end it in the stairwell. {coworker} nods: 'Professional.' The coffee orders stop.

title: Drinks after work. {coworker} leans in: 'Your partner never has to know about tonight.'

outcomes.text: You pay your tab and go home. Your partner made too much pasta. Good call.

options.label: Stay for one more
options.cost: Your partner's trust, if it gets out

outcomes.text: One more becomes three. Nothing happens. Probably. You get home at 2.

later.text: Remember 'one more' with {coworker}? Your partner saw the photos. They have questions.

outcomes.text: You tell them everything. They're quiet, then: 'Thanks for telling me.' You order takeout together.
